jurisdiction.name: Guinea
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Guinea has no AI-specific law or published AI strategy. Its only binding text with an AI-relevant rule is the 2016 law on cybersecurity and personal data protection, whose Article 27 limits decisions based solely on automated profiling. A national AI roadmap for 2026-2035 is listed as validated in December 2025 with UNDP support, and a national AI strategy has been announced; neither is yet verified from an official text. The Simandou 2040 development plan laws adopted in March 2026 cover digital infrastructure but contain no AI provisions. The digital ministry leads AI policy work, with the information systems security agency (ANSSI) responsible for cybersecurity.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
National Agency for Information Systems Security (ANSSI)
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed again on 18 October 2026: the Official Journal, the Secretariat-General of Government (laws, decrees, texts open for comment, Council of Ministers reports), the Presidency, the Prime Minister's office, the government portal, the cybersecurity agency and the central bank were checked. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material from the digital ministry, the National Assembly, the telecom regulator and the data protection authority. The national AI roadmap 2026-2035, the planned AI strategy and the data strategy remain leads pending official publication.

instruments.official_title: Loi N° L/2016/037/AN relative à la cyber-sécurité et la protection des données à caractère personnel en République de Guinée
instruments.english_title: Law No. L/2016/037/AN on Cybersecurity and the Protection of Personal Data in the Republic of Guinea
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly (promulgated by the President of the Republic)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 26 July 2016; Article 65 states it enters into force from its promulgation and is to be published in the Journal Officiel. The ANSSI publishes the signed text on its laws page. Article 27 restricts decisions based solely on automated processing that evaluates personality or produces a profile. Controllers had one year from promulgation to comply (Article 63). No AI-specific amendment found as of October 2026.
instruments.summary: Guinea's framework law on cybersecurity (first part, cybercrime offences and security of information systems) and personal data protection (second part, 65 articles). The data protection part requires declarations or authorisations with the authority in charge of personal data protection, sets processing principles (consent, purpose limitation, accuracy, security, transfer rules) and data subject rights of access, rectification and objection. Article 27 bars judicial decisions assessing a person's behaviour from being based on automated processing intended to evaluate their personality, and bars administrative or private decisions assessing human behaviour from being based solely on automated processing that defines the person's profile.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Guinean text with an explicit rule on automated decision-making and profiling (Article 27); governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.
